rule_metadata.rule_name_english: Madd 'Arid lis-Sukoon (Temporary Sukoon Madd) & Madd Badal (Substitution Madd)
rule_metadata.description: Comprehensive rules covering the 2-to-6 count temporary sukoon lengthening upon stopping and the fixed 2-count substitution lengthening originating from a preceded Hamzah.

madd_arid_lissukun.name: Madd 'Arid lis-Sukoon (Temporary Sukoon Madd)
madd_arid_lissukun.definition: Occurs when a Madd letter is followed by a letter whose original vowel is temporarily replaced by a Sukoon because the reciter stops (Waqf) on that word.
madd_arid_lissukun.ruling: Permissible lengthening of **2, 4, or 6 counts** (Harakat), provided the reciter maintains a consistent choice throughout their recitation session.

madd_badal.name: Madd Badal (Substitution Madd)
madd_badal.definition: Occurs when a Hamzah precedes a Madd letter in the same word (originally two Hamzahs where the second vowelled Hamzah was converted into a weak Madd letter to ease pronunciation).
madd_badal.ruling: Fixed lengthening of exactly **2 counts** according to Hafs 'an 'Asim.

sub_divisions.fixed_origin: Derived from patterns like أَاْمَنَ -> آمَنَ.

practical_examples.breakdown: The Noon of Al-'Alameen receives a temporary Sukoon upon stopping; the preceding Ya Madd is stretched 2, 4, or 6 counts.
Hamzah precedes an Alif Madd; extended for exactly 2 counts.
Hamzah with Kasrah precedes Ya Madd; extended for 2 counts.

assessment_bank.question: What defines Madd 'Arid lis-Sukoon?
options: A Madd letter followed by a temporary Sukoon caused by stopping on a word
A Madd letter followed by a permanent Shaddah
A Hamzah preceding a Madd letter

assessment_bank.question: What are the permissible lengths (counts) for Madd 'Arid lis-Sukoon?
Why is it called 'Arid' (Temporary)?
options: Because the Sukoon on the final letter only appears when stopping (Waqf)
Because it uses a temporary vowel
Because it is a weak rule

assessment_bank.question: What defines Madd Badal (Substitution Madd)?
options: A Hamzah preceding a Madd letter in the same word
A Madd letter followed by a Hamzah

assessment_bank.question: How many counts is Madd Badal lengthened according to Hafs?
Why is it called 'Badal' (Substitution)?
options: Because a second vowelled Hamzah was substituted/converted into a Madd letter for ease of articulation
Because letters are substituted across words

assessment_bank.question: In the word 'الْعَالَمِينَ', if you stop on it at the end of an ayah, what rule applies to the Ya Madd?
In the word 'آمَنَ', what Tajweed rule applies to the opening Alif?
What happens if a reciter chooses a 4-count length for Madd 'Arid lis-Sukoon in verse 1 of Surah Al-Fatihah?
options: They should maintain that exact 4-count tempo consistently throughout their recitation session
They must switch to 6 counts immediately

assessment_bank.question: In 'إِيمَانًا', what letter of Madd follows the initial Hamzah?
What is the historical origin of the spelling in Madd Badal words like 'آمَنَ'?
options: Originally أَاْمَنَ (two Hamzahs), where the second was changed to Alif

assessment_bank.question: If you continue reciting past 'رَبِّ الْعَالَمِينَ' without stopping (Wasl), what does the Madd 'Arid lis-Sukoon revert to?
options: Madd Tabii (2 counts only, because the Sukoon disappears when unvowelled or vowel-connected)

assessment_bank.question: Which of the following words contains a Madd Badal?
What is the correct count for Madd Badal across all authentic transmission paths for Hafs?
In 'نَسْتَعِينُ', when stopping at the end of the ayah, how is it categorized?
Does Madd Badal occur when the Hamzah comes AFTER the Madd letter?
options: No, that is Muttasil or Munfasil; Badal requires the Hamzah to precede the Madd letter

assessment_bank.question: In 'آمَنُوا', how many Madd rules are present?
options: Two (Madd Badal on the first Alif = 2 counts, Madd Tabii on the Waw = 2 counts)

assessment_bank.question: What is the primary objective of Madd 'Arid lis-Sukoon when pausing in recitation?
options: To allow a smooth, melodious, and graceful breathing pause at verse endings

assessment_bank.question: If a reciter stops on 'الرَّحِيمِ', what is the sound produced on the Meem?
options: A temporary Sukoon replacing the original Kasrah

assessment_bank.question: In 'الْخَاسِرِينَ', stopping at the end creates which Tajweed rule?
Can Madd Badal appear in the middle of a word rather than just the beginning?
options: Yes, such as in رِئَاسَةٍ or similar constructs where Hamzah precedes Madd
No, only at the absolute start of words

assessment_bank.question: What error does an AI evaluation engine flag if a student changes their 'Arid lis-Sukoon length erratically from 2 counts to 6 counts mid-ayah?
In 'ءَادَمُ', what rule applies to the Hamzah followed by Alif?
How does Madd Badal differ from Madd Tabii in spelling notation?
options: Badal is written with a Hamzah before the Madd letter (sometimes as a prolonged Maddah sign over Hamzah), whereas Tabii has no preceding Hamzah

assessment_bank.question: In 'الْحَكِيمُ', when stopping at the end, what is the minimum recommended length for Arid lis-Sukoon for standard practice?
What happens to Madd Badal if the word is connected to the next word in recitation?
options: It remains a fixed 2 counts because the Hamzah-preceded-by-Madd structure is internal to the word

assessment_bank.question: Which of the following is an example of Madd Badal with Waw?
Why is Madd Badal considered one of the easiest secondary Madds to master?
options: Because its duration is fixed rigidly at 2 counts, just like Madd Tabii

assessment_bank.question: In 'سَمِيعٌ بَصِيرٌ', if you stop on 'بَصِيرٌ', what rule is triggered?
What is the relationship between Waqf (stopping) and Madd 'Arid lis-Sukoon?
options: Waqf is the direct trigger that creates the temporary Sukoon, activating the Arid rule

assessment_bank.question: In 'ءَالْآنَ', how many rules are combined?
options: Both Madd Badal (on the first Hamzah) and Madd Lazim (on the second Alif)

assessment_bank.question: If a student recites Madd Badal with 6 counts, what feedback should be given?
options: Madd Badal is strictly 2 counts; reserve 6 counts for Madd Lazim

assessment_bank.question: In 'الْمُؤْمِنِينَ', when pausing at the end of a verse, what rule applies?
What is the phonetic sound of Madd Badal when recited correctly?
options: A clean, unhurried 2-count vowel expansion directly following a glottal Hamzah

assessment_bank.question: In 'وَأُوْلَئِكَ', does Madd Badal apply to 'أُوْلَئِكَ'?
options: Yes, the Hamzah precedes a Waw Madd, forming a 2-count Madd Badal

assessment_bank.question: Why is mastering Madd 'Arid lis-Sukoon essential for Quranic recitation beauty?
options: Because almost every verse ends with a pause requiring graceful Arid lengthening for recitation rhythm
Because it is required for spelling
Because it replaces all other rules

assessment_bank.question: If a reciter uses 2 counts for Arid in verse 1 and 6 counts for Arid in verse 2 of the same sitting, what is the ruling?
options: Permissible in Islamic tajweed schools, though consistency within a single reading session is preferred

assessment_bank.question: Which two secondary Madds both share a standard baseline duration of 2 counts?
In 'مَآبٍ', when stopping on the word, how many rules interact?
options: Madd Badal (fixed 2 counts on the first part) and Madd Arid lis-Sukoon (2, 4, or 6 counts on the final pause)

assessment_bank.question: Summarize the core definitions of Madd 'Arid lis-Sukoon and Madd Badal:
options: 'Arid is 2-4-6 counts upon pausing due to temporary Sukoon; Badal is fixed 2 counts when a Hamzah precedes a Madd letter
